title: DDR4_Lite: DDR4-style line controller: 4 banks with open-row tracking, ACT / RD / WR / PRE / PREA / REF on DDR4 pins, tRCD / tRP / tRC / tRAS / tRRD / tWR / tWTR / tRFC / tREFI, BL8 x16 line bursts, MR file with CL / CWL, all-bank refresh

regs.name: CMD
regs.desc: Host command beat; writing CMD2 sends it: a command, or one of the 8 data beats that follow a WRITE

fdesc.hcmd: command (see the notes); ignored on a data beat
fdesc.haddr: host address (see the notes); ignored on a data beat
fdesc.hwdata: MRW value (bits 7:0), or the data beat of a WRITE (beat 0 = line bits 15:0)

fields.desc: {8'h0, MR value} after an MRR (also carries read beats while a READ drains)

regs.name: RLINE
regs.desc: Line of the last READ (RLINE0 = bits 31:0)

fields.desc: the 128-bit line of the last READ, held until the next READ completes

irqs.name: DONE
irqs.desc: a command finished (READ: RLINE holds the line; MRR: RDATA holds the value)

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: a command was rejected (out-of-range address, illegal code) or a refresh overran; the core holds this until reset, so the bit cannot be cleared before then

notes: haddr: [8:7] bank, [17:9] row, [6:4] line; [31:18] must be 0. hcmd 0 NOP, 1 READ line, 2 WRITE line (then 8 data beats), 3 MRW (haddr[2:0], hwdata[7:0]; MR0 bit 7 is a self-clearing DLL reset), 4 MRR, 5 REFRESH; 6 and 7 are rejected.
The DRAM pins (ck_t, ck_c, cke, cs_n, act_n, ras_n, cas_n, we_n, ba, addr, dq, dqs) and the command trace pass through unchanged.
The core's own verification (pin-level checker, 100% coverage) is tb/cov/DDR4_Lite_sva.sv with tb/DDR4_Lite_tb.sv; this wrapper test drives the core only through the registers.
